Description: Enable Software Engineers to define, configure, and maintain feature flags with unique keys, default states, and multi-environment overrides (Dev, Staging, Prod) to prevent configuration drift and safely test features.

Enable engineering teams to configure granular user cohort targeting (e.g. beta groups, user ID attributes) and deterministic percentage rollouts (0-100%) to safely limit blast radius and validate releases.

Summary: Epic 3: Governance, Approval Workflows & Audit Logging
Description: Provide Release Managers with an approval gate to inspect configuration diffs, enforce 4-eyes principle before production changes, and maintain an immutable audit trail for compliance and rollbacks.

Summary: Epic 4: High-Performance Evaluation & Real-Time SDK Sync
Description: Deliver low-latency flag evaluation API (< 15ms p95) and push instantaneous configuration changes to connected client SDKs via persistent WebSockets/streaming connections without requiring client redeployments.

Summary: US-01: Create Feature Flag with Unique Key and Default State
Description:
As a Software Engineer, I want to create a feature flag with a unique key, description, and default state (enabled/disabled), so that my client application can reference the flag unambiguously.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Submitting a flag key that already exists is rejected with a duplicate-key error.
- A unique key is created and appears in the flag list within 2 seconds.
- Default state is properly persisted.

As a Software Engineer, I want to configure a percentage rollout (0-100%) based on a deterministic hash of user IDs, so that I can gradually roll out features and minimize blast radius.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Setting rollout to 25% results in 25% (+/-2%) of 10,000 simulated user IDs receiving enabled state.
- Cohort assignment for a given user ID remains strictly deterministic across repeated evaluations.

Summary: US-03: Evaluate User Targeting Rules for Cohorts
Description:
As a Software Engineer, I want to define targeting rules based on user attributes (e.g., User ID hash, beta cohort membership), so that specific user segments receive early access to features.

Acceptance Criteria:
- A user in the targeted cohort receives the enabled flag.
- Any user outside the cohort receives the fallback/disabled flag accurately.

Summary: US-04: Optimize Evaluation API Engine to Sub-15ms Latency
Description:
As a Software Engineer, I want the flag evaluation engine to execute in under 15ms, so that integrating flag checks into client critical paths adds negligible overhead.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Benchmarking tests confirm p95 latency under 15 ms under peak load.
- Memory-cached lookup prevents unnecessary database queries.

Summary: US-05: Implement Client SDK Local Cache and Fallback
Description:
As a Client Application Developer, I want the SDK to maintain a local in-memory cache with fallback defaults, so that temporary network dropouts do not break host application features.

Acceptance Criteria:
- In-memory evaluations return within 1ms during offline scenarios.
- System logs a warning and falls back to default state safely if disconnected.

As a Software Engineer, I want to define environment-specific overrides (Development, Staging, Production), so that I can test a flag in lower environments without exposing it in Production.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Setting Production override to OFF while Staging is ON returns disabled for Production and enabled for Staging.
- No configuration leaks across environment boundaries.

Summary: US-07: Draft Flag Revisions and Preview Visual Configuration Diff
Description:
As a Software Engineer, I want to save configuration changes as pending revisions and view a visual diff against the published state, so that I can verify my modifications before asking for approval.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Pending drafts are saved without affecting live client evaluation.
- Visual diff clearly contrasts old vs new rules, percentages, and overrides.

Summary: US-08: Release Manager Review, Approval Gate, and Validation
Description:
As a Release Manager, I want to review, approve, or reject pending flag changes with validation checks, so that only verified and safe flag configurations reach production.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Only authenticated users with Release Manager role can publish.
- Schema, consistency, and 0-100% ranges are validated prior to publishing.
- Rejection records reasons and leaves the live version untouched.

Summary: US-09: Immutable Audit Logging and One-Click Rollback
Description:
As a Release Manager, I want all configuration changes recorded in an immutable audit log with one-click rollback, so that team actions are traceable for security compliance and fast disaster recovery.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Every successful publish creates an unalterable audit entry with approver, timestamp, and previous value.
- One-click rollback restores prior published version in under 3 seconds.

Summary: US-10: Real-Time Flag State Streaming to Connected SDKs
Description:
As a Client Application / SDK Developer, I want updated flag states pushed via real-time WebSocket streaming, so that clients reflect new configs within 5 seconds without redeployment.

Acceptance Criteria:
- 95% of connected SDK instances receive new values within 5 seconds of publish.
- Connection drop triggers auto-reconnect with latest version snapshot.
